paper_diagnosis: Sino-orbital aspergillosis in a kidney transplant recipient
disease_label_per_paper: Proven invasive sino-orbital aspergillosis caused by Aspergillus flavus in a kidney transplant recipient
paper_diagnosis_source_text_value: proven invasive sino-orbital aspergillosis resulting in irreversible loss of vision despite surgical management and antifungal therapy
presentation_summary: Kidney transplant recipient with diabetic nephropathy on tacrolimus, methylprednisolone, and mycophenolate mofetil.
Presented with fatigue, photophobia, right hemicranial headache, and progressive right-eye vision loss.
Exam showed ptosis, unreactive pupil, complete afferent pupillary defect, total paralysis of the right eye, and no light perception.
CT showed pansinusitis with calcifications, chronic bone thickening, and focal osteolysis of the right optic canal floor.
MRI showed inflammatory extension to the sphenoid fissure and encasement of the intracanal segment of the right optic nerve without intracranial extension.
Surgical pathology showed fungal hyphae; culture and PCR identified Aspergillus flavus.
